criteria.name: reading-pleasure
criteria.text: Reading pleasure: how much a reader would enjoy the act of reading this — voice, wit, craft, momentum — independent of anything taken away from it.

criteria.name: mistake-prevention
criteria.text: Mistake prevention: how likely a reader who never reads this ends up making a specific costly decision or holding a specific false belief that this text would have prevented.

criteria.name: challenge-to-priors
criteria.text: Challenge to priors: how much a reader who currently disagrees with the central claim would be forced to update or sharpen their view after reading it — the text as the strongest opposing case, not merely new information.

criteria.name: reader-empowerment
criteria.text: Reader empowerment: the reader finishes more capable — holding a tool, a move, or a distinction they can apply — rather than merely informed, entertained, or alarmed.

criteria.name: source-uniqueness
criteria.text: Source uniqueness: how hard it would be to get this text's payload anywhere else — first-hand data, direct experience, or a synthesis no other single text provides — as opposed to content many other texts also deliver.

criteria.name: misleading-if-trusted
criteria.text: Misleading if trusted: the chance that a reader who takes this text at face value ends up confidently wrong — through its framing, its omissions, or certainty it has not earned — regardless of how careful it looks.
